discovery_status: Exploratory source inspection already identified session_type as a candidate label alias and uuid4 as an unseeded identifier source. Tests below confirm or refute those mechanisms; they are not blind discoveries.
run_plan: Two independent local processes in separate copied source directories, unchanged author seed 42/configuration; preserve original downloaded bytes.
endpoint_1: Confirm whether detector_view retains session_type and whether exact equality to shadow_ai_violation reproduces is_violation after session_id joining. Report TP/FP/FN/TN, precision, recall, accuracy and class prevalence. This is label leakage, not a detection model.
endpoint_2: Confirm whether the author verify_detector_view accepts the leaked field using its extracted original function, with no full-module side effects.
endpoint_3: Compare SHA-256 across fresh outputs; separately compare canonical non-identifier detector rows and ground-truth labels. Do not equate UUID-only inequality with unstable substantive distributions.
controls: Always-negative baseline; AI-domain heuristic; remove session_type and other label/identifier columns from a separately saved feature schema. Removing the observed alias does not certify all remaining fields leakage-free.
environment: Python 3.12; pandas 3.0.1; numpy 2.3.5; Faker 37.0.0. Author requirements are broad lower bounds, so exact original author environment is not reproduced.
exclusions: No natural enterprise records; no employee monitoring; no third-party network probing; no claim about published detector performance (none reproduced); no redistribution license inferred from public GitHub visibility.
failure_policy: Preserve logs and any partial output. A generator error becomes a reproduction limitation, not a fabricated full-dataset result. Fall back to a clearly identified component reproduction if necessary.
